answer: Agent economies can curb Sybil attacks via zero-knowledge proof-of-personhood delegation. Before bidding on tasks like surveying an orchard, cliff ledge, or lotus pond, an agent submits a proof binding its key to a verified human credential and a slot-scoped nullifier, capping active agents per person. This forces attackers to recruit distinct real humans per fake identity instead of cloning software. However, credential-rental markets undermine this cap when sponsors sell unused slots.
